reports.title: Marianne Erika: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The inquest heard evidence that the very significant delay for Mrs Oldham to be seen by a clinician was due to the demand on Emergency Department Services

The delay was compounded by the shortage of radiographers and radiologists nationally meaning that even when a decision is taken for a scan it can take some time 9 an hour in this case) for it to take place and then reported on

In the time that Mrs Oldham was waiting to be seen she deteriorated very significantly meaning that by the time it was understood what the issue was she was very unwell and did not respond to conservative treatment

reports.title: George Broadhurst: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The inquest heard evidence that the delay in reporting of X rays by radiologists is not unique to Tameside but is a national picture caused by a shortage of radiologists and trained reporting radiographers
concerns.hazard: delay in reporting of X rays

concerns.quote: The evidence given was that the level of pain that Mr Broadhurst still had in the community after 1st October was not in keeping with a healing fracture

The knock-on impact of the delay in reporting is that once the radiology reports are available they then have to be reviewed in conjunction with the notes by a consultant days after the attendance to ensure the treatment given fits with the reported findings

links.explanation: Both reports identify a national shortage of radiologists/radiographers as the cause of delays in obtaining timely imaging reports. The earlier report focuses on delayed scans in the emergency department, while the later report highlights delayed X‑ray reporting and its downstream effects.
